Shingle Roof Cost Guide

National Average Roof Cost: For a typical 2,000 square foot single-family home (25 to 28 roofing squares including pitch and waste allowance), a complete shingle roof replacement generally costs between $8,200 and $14,500 for standard architectural asphalt shingles. Premium materials such as stone-coated metal, synthetic composite, or natural slate range from $16,000 to over $45,000.

Understanding the Labor vs. Material Split

On an average residential steep-slope roofing replacement, your total contractor bid is distributed across three primary cost categories:

  • Labor & Craftsmanship (45% – 60%): Covers skilled tear-off, decking prep, underlayment rolling, shingle nailing, metal flashing bending, staging, and cleanup.
  • Materials & Accessories (35% – 45%): Encompasses shingles, synthetic underlayment, starter shingles, ridge caps, drip edges, fasteners, and ice-and-water membranes.
  • Permits, Disposal & Overhead (10% – 15%): Covers municipal building inspection permits, roll-off dumpster rental, landfill tipping fees, and contractor insurance liabilities.
